title: A foundation for systematic analysis of transformers and RNNs for tractography
abstract: arXiv:2610.01894v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising approach for improving diffusion MRI (dMRI) tractography, a task that remains limited by the intrinsic tension between local diffusion information and global anatomical plausibility. In this work, we systematically evaluate recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and Transformer models for iterative tractography, with particular attention to training strategies, input representations (including convolutional neural network (CNN)-based embeddings and end-of-sequence (EOS) tokens), and hyperparameter selection. We introduce a generation-validation phase enabling supervision at the streamline level during training, allowing supervision despite the mismatch between local loss functions and global streamline quality. Using the ISMRM2015 tractography challenge dataset, our models achieve the highest reported performance to date. Through controlled experiments, we quantify the impact of missing bundles,

translated_title: 用于纤维束成像的Transformer与循环神经网络系统性分析的基础
translated_abstract: 机器学习（ML）已成为改进扩散磁共振成像（dMRI）纤维束成像的一种有前景的方法，但该任务始终受到局部扩散信息与全局解剖学合理性之间内在张力的限制。在这项工作中，我们系统地评估了循环神经网络（RNN）和Transformer模型在迭代纤维束成像中的表现，特别关注训练策略、输入表示（包括基于卷积神经网络（CNN）的嵌入和序列结束标记）以及超参数选择。我们引入了一种生成-验证阶段，能够在训练过程中实现流线级别的监督，从而在局部损失函数与全局流线质量不匹配的情况下仍能进行有效监督。使用ISMRM2015纤维束成像挑战赛数据集，我们的模型实现了迄今报告的最高性能。通过受控实验，我们量化了缺失纤维束的影响……
tldr: 该论文系统评估了RNN和Transformer在迭代纤维束成像中的应用，提出了一种生成-验证阶段以实现流线级别的监督学习，并在ISMRM2015挑战赛数据集上取得了迄今最高的性能。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically evaluates RNNs and Transformers for iterative tractography, introduces a generation-validation phase enabling streamline-level supervision, and achieves the highest reported performance on the ISMRM2015 tractography challenge dataset.
